title: Chiral classical and quantum acoustics with hole-spin qubits
authors: Zhanning Wang, Yongtao Li, Nelson E. Rivas, Gonzalo García, Irene Castro, Rubén Seoane Souto, Daniel Ramos, José C. Abadillo-Uriel
abstract: Gate-defined hole spins combine strong spin-orbit coupling with exceptional strain sensitivity, making surface acoustic waves a natural route to remote, phase-coherent control. We show that counterpropagating surface acoustic waves can differ in coupling strength and in whether they predominantly drive spin rotations or modulate the qubit frequency. We call the transverse transition-strength imbalance spin-acoustic chirality and show that it is tunable through gate-controlled reshaping of the dot confinement. Combining a multiband Luttinger-Kohn Hamiltonian with the Bir-Pikus description of strain and 3D piezoelectric finite-element simulations, we obtain the acoustic g-matrix modulation governing coherent SAW driving. Quantizing the same strain-mediated interaction yields the corresponding single-phonon coupling, and a generalized anisotropic Rabi interaction with co-rotating, counter-rotating, and longitudinal components, linking classical chirality to quantum anisotropy and directional one-phonon emission. Magnetic field orientation and dot shape tune the acoustic chirality and operator selectivity. We illustrate this framework through bichromatic coherence protection and phonon-mediated heralded Bell-state initialization.
summary: This paper theoretically models the interaction between hole-spin qubits and surface acoustic waves (SAWs) using a detailed Hamiltonian approach. It introduces the concept of 'spin-acoustic chirality' to quantify how the direction of the SAW affects the qubit's spin dynamics. The results show that this coupling is highly tunable via external electric and magnetic fields, offering a pathway for coherent quantum control using acoustic phonons.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified description linking classical acoustic chirality to quantum anisotropy in hole-spin qubits driven by surface acoustic waves (SAWs). It aims to understand how counterpropagating SAWs differentially couple to the qubit spin.
main_result: The coupling strength and directional chirality are tunable by electrostatic gating and magnetic field orientation, allowing for precise control over longitudinal versus transverse qubit driving components.
method: The authors combine a microscopic Luttinger-Kohn Hamiltonian with Bir-Pikus strain theory and 3D finite-element simulations to derive the acoustic g-matrix modulation.
model_or_system: The system involves gate-defined hole spins in a quantum well coupled to Rayleigh-type surface acoustic waves. The theoretical framework uses the LKBP model to describe strain-mediated coupling to the qubit's g-matrix.
key_observables: Acoustic chirality ($\chi$), directional balance ($\Lambda_{TL,\xi}$), and the modulation of the qubit g-matrix components.
important_parameters: Acoustic wave frequency (e.g., 2 GHz), magnetic field orientation ($	heta_B$), and SAW propagation angle ($	heta_{SAW}$).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on projecting the full six-band LKBP Hamiltonian onto the lowest Zeeman-split doublet and uses leading-order approximations in HH-LH mixing.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the SAW path through the device structure and the coupling of two quantum dots to a confined SAW mode.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical setup and the microscopic Hamiltonian (LKBP model) to deriving the strain-induced g-matrix modulation. It then quantizes this interaction, analyzing the resulting anisotropic Rabi coupling components, and finally discusses control mechanisms via gating and magnetic fields.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, physically tunable mechanism for coupling solid-state qubits to acoustic phonons, which is crucial for developing scalable quantum memories and gates using phononics.
